title: 32-byte record index reference
summary: Recovered 0x41dfb0 as a genuine thiscall member with explicit output pointer and returned output address. Loads owner at this+8, metadata at this+4, adds metadata+8 to the index modulo 2^32, scales by 32, adds owner+12, then writes the original table identity, computed record address and owner to the 12-byte output. All input loads precede output stores. No allocation, record dereference or bounds check occurs. Direct Game.exe disassembly and nearby callers corroborate the accepted reference; callers read record+8. Implementation compiled with GCC and the supplied VS2013 compiler.
test_description: 4000 original-versus-recovered comparisons: ten base indices by ten indices by four record-array address values by ten output placements. Includes zero, ordinary indices, sign-bit patterns, addition/shift/address wrapping, null-valued computed addresses, and output overlapping this, metadata or owner fields. Checks returned pointer, all three output words, and every untouched word in the 256-byte arena. Installs initialized test-owned FS backing and verifies its head after each original call. Oracle linked at 0x41dfb0; its 40 bytes independently compared with Game.exe.
known_limits: Layouts and stored addresses model the original 32-bit address space; a 64-bit port must supply address translation or deliberately redesign layouts and dispatch.
The fixed table address is preserved as data identity; table methods, relocation and higher-level record semantics are outside the assigned scope.
Valid readable metadata/owner and writable output are required. Invalid-pointer faults and arbitrary unaligned inputs are not tested.
No bounds checks exist in the original. Computed record addresses are not dereferenced by this routine.
Behavioral validation and local MSVC compilation do not establish matching machine code.
